transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. I'm here because I feel like I'm always running hot. It's like I have this motor inside me that I just can't shut off, no matter what I do. And lately, that's been getting me into some trouble at the firehouse, so I figured I needed to come in and get it checked out.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are racing or that you don't need much sleep because you feel so energized?

No, not really. I mean, my mind can get pretty busy with all the stuff I need to do, but I wouldn't say my thoughts are racing like they're out of control. And I definitely need my sleep. If I don't get enough rest, especially with the shifts at the firehouse, I'm pretty wiped out. I don't get that super energized feeling where I can just skip sleeping.
Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even if just for a few days?

No, I haven't really felt like that. I mean, I get frustrated sometimes, especially when I mess up at work because I can't sit still or focus, but I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or down. I still like doing the things I usually do, like hanging out with the guys or working on my truck. I definitely haven't lost interest in any of that.
Do you ever feel unusually worried, tense, or restless, even when there's no immediate reason to be?

Not really. I mean, I'm definitely restless, like I said about the motor feeling, but it's not because I'm worried or tense about anything. I don't sit around feeling anxious or stressed out for no reason. It's just a physical thing, like my body always needs to be moving, not that my mind is worried about something bad happening.
Have you found yourself acting impulsively or taking risks recently, like doing things without thinking about the consequences?

No, I wouldn't say I'm taking risks like that. I mean, my job is inherently risky, being a firefighter, but I follow protocol. I don't just jump into a burning building without thinking. Outside of work, I don't really do anything crazy either. Sometimes I might speak before I think, like blurting something out, but I'm not out there gambling or driving recklessly or anything like that.
Have you always had this feeling of restlessness, even going back to when you were a kid, or is this something that started more recently?

Yeah, it's pretty much always been there. My mom says I was exactly like this back in grade school. I was always the kid getting up out of my seat, blurting out answers before the teacher finished asking, and just generally driving everyone crazy. I was always losing my homework, too, and getting notes sent home about my behavior, even though the teachers always said I was bright enough to actually do the work. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new thing.
